rules_to_explain: The 20 areas as collapsible blocks in the PHC's order (GET /phc/cpsa areas); inside, one row per document: its number and title, kind badge (Format / Policy / Register / Notification / Upload / Guideline), the four status dots of the declaration (available, staff trained, implemented, uploaded: green / red / grey for not applicable) with the reason on hover.

Downloads per row: 'PHC template' (template_url: the Commission's own Word, Excel or PDF file as published, when there is one), 'Filled (PDF)' (pdf_url: one click, one PDF, filled from the records) and, for the four lists of CPSA 1, 'Filled (Excel)' (xlsx_url: the PHC accepts them only in Excel). Null url = no such button.

PDFs only, never a ZIP: follow download_mode (the user's preference, PUT /settings/me pdf_download): Separate = the per-row buttons; Combined = one 'Download all CPSA documents' button (combined_pdf_url) with a contents page. The declaration (Annexure A, declaration_pdf_url) and the PHC's guidelines (guidelines_url) have their own buttons in the header.
Period picker (date_from, date_to; default the last 90 days, at most 366): the registers print for it; policies as of today.

CPSA_DOCUMENT_UNAVAILABLE on a download: show details.reason next to the row (no record review closed yet; nothing to fill: download the PHC's file). A register naming patients is logged like a read of a record.

The header counts (available / trained / implemented / uploaded of the applicable documents) are the hospital's progress to a signed declaration; the quality officer fixes the red reasons before the head signs.

The status answers 'Yes' only from evidence in the records (a signed version, a notification with its members, register entries in the period, a recorded display, a valid licence), never because a document can be printed: never relabel a red dot as 'ready'. A document of a service not run here shows grey (applies false: not applicable).

Declaration rows (each document's rows): the PHC's wording, then Available / Staff trained / Implemented / Uploaded, each showing value, a 'from the records' tag until a person confirmed it (confirmation null), and the reason; a fixed column is a plain NA. Header: declaration_rows_confirmed of declaration_rows.

Row action 'Confirm or correct' (msds.cpsa.manage) on each answerable column: Yes / No / Not applicable, the reason (required) and, with Yes, where the evidence is kept (required: the register, the file, the photo) -> POST /phc/cpsa/declaration/answers {document_key, row_no, question, answer, reason, evidence}; the answer is the row as it now reads. 'Withdraw' sends answer null (the records' answer counts again). History: GET /phc/cpsa/declaration/answers?document_key=. Before 'Declaration (PDF)', warn when declaration_rows_confirmed < declaration_rows: the unconfirmed answers print with * and the head signs the whole form under the PHC Act.

Row action 'Record upload' (msds.cpsa.manage): uploaded_on (today), the portal's reference, a note -> POST /phc/cpsa/uploads; the uploaded dot turns green; GET /phc/cpsa/uploads?document_key= shows the history.

Services declared (CPSA 1.2, Annexure B): a checklist of the PHC's services by group (GET /phc/services) with a remarks box per line and 'Others' lines the hospital types (is_listed false, with the group); Save -> PUT /phc/services (the whole list each time). A listed name must be spelled as the PHC spells it (VALIDATION_ERROR otherwise). The filled Excel and PDF of the list follow the declaration at once.

screen_requirements.title: Purpose and audience
screen_requirements.instruction:
Explain what this screen accomplishes, when to use it, who uses it and how to open it. State the patient, visit,
shift or other context the user must verify. Name the expected result in staff language.

screen_requirements.title: Step by step (one per task, where to click)
screen_requirements.instruction:
For every supported task give prerequisites, permissions or approvals, exact navigation and control labels,
what to enter or select, validation, the ordered steps and how to recognize completion. Include demo screenshots,
printed output and the next task or handover. Link to the corresponding workspace FAQ answer.

screen_requirements.title: Every control and its effects
screen_requirements.instruction:
Maintain a control inventory covering buttons, fields, selectors, tabs, menus, filters, sorting, scanners, shortcuts,
dialogs and navigation. For each user-facing control explain its label and purpose, when it is available, required
input, immediate effect, whether it saves or only changes the view, any confirmation, and what cancellation does.
Describe resulting data/state changes, notifications, printed output and consequences for other staff where relevant.
Include controls without API calls. Group repeated controls only when their behaviour is genuinely identical.

screen_requirements.title: States and feedback
screen_requirements.instruction:
Explain loading, no results, pending approval, success, stale data, denied actions and unavailable services. Describe
automatic realtime updates and how staff recognize that displayed information has changed. Explain disabled controls
and how to meet their prerequisites. Document only states and effects the implemented UI and backend support.

screen_requirements.title: Messages, mistakes and recovery
screen_requirements.instruction:
Explain the messages staff can encounter, why an action is refused and the permitted next step. Cover corrections,
duplicate clicks, a lost reply, concurrent changes, leaving unsaved work, session expiry, lost connection and printer
or scanner problems where applicable. Say what may have been saved, what to check before retrying and whom to contact.
Never promise unsupported undo or automatic offline submission. Use staff wording, not API paths or JSON.

screen_requirements.title: Language and visual examples
screen_requirements.instruction:
Supply English and Urdu pages matching the app's labels and reading direction, with legible demo-data screenshots
for each task and no real patient information. Keep terminology consistent across UI, FAQs and screenshots. Record
translation review status; a draft must not be represented as approved clinical wording.

screen_requirements.title: Related help and delivery
screen_requirements.instruction:
Link to the role's workspace guide, related tasks and handovers. F1 and contextual Help must open this screen's page.
Verify offline access, search, deep links, print-friendly output and the server's permission filtering. Update the
page, control inventory and FAQ links in the same release as the UI; retain the review evidence required by Q6.

workspace_requirements.title: A day in each role
workspace_requirements.instruction:
Explain the workspace's purpose and each role that uses it, how to enter or switch workspaces, start and finish a
shift, and the typical order of work. State what the role may do and what requires another role, without presenting
role names as the app's permission checks. Include shared and linked screens needed to finish the job.

workspace_requirements.title: Complete job-task index
workspace_requirements.instruction:
List every job task supported for each role in this workspace. Map each task to a detailed FAQ answer and the
relevant screen instructions. Reconcile this inventory with the catalogue's tasks, permissions, playbooks, shared
screens and the actual UI, including frontend-only tasks. Do not claim that a list of API operations alone covers
everything staff need to learn. Mark unsupported requests explicitly rather than inventing a workflow.

workspace_requirements.title: Detailed role-specific FAQ
workspace_requirements.instruction:
For every supported task answer "How do I ...?" in the user's language. Each answer must give when to use it,
prerequisites, exact navigation and labels, ordered steps, what each action changes, the expected outcome, common
mistakes/refusals and recovery, approvals or handovers and links to screen help. Include exceptions and follow-up
questions from the tested journey. Shared answers may be linked, but distinguish differences between roles and
permissions. Short generic advice or an unexplained link is insufficient.

This FAQ is compulsory for every supported role in the workspace, including its shared tasks. Missing answers,
missing English/Urdu coverage or an unreviewed FAQ keep the workspace unfinished, even when its API calls work.

The FAQ answers at least every question of `faq_seed` for the workspace (`GET /meta/handbook?workspace=<code>` →
`faq_seed`; the MCP server's `get_handbook_outline` gives the same list): one per error a screen of the workspace can
meet and one per state machine its screens move. They are the minimum, not the whole FAQ.

workspace_requirements.title: Handovers, exceptions and troubleshooting
workspace_requirements.instruction:
Explain what to do when work is waiting for another role, who acts next, how to find the request later and how to
recognize completion or refusal. Cover the workspace's applicable problems: unavailable devices or network, a locked
session, conflicting edits, a correction, an uncertain submission and an unfinished shift. Refer to the hospital's
approved downtime procedure where required; do not invent clinical or financial policy.

workspace_requirements.title: Glossary and guided practice
workspace_requirements.instruction:
Define the workspace's staff-facing terms consistently with the UI. Provide a complete practice journey using newly
created synthetic records on the DEV server, covering the relevant screens, role boundaries and help navigation.
A named human reviewer must follow the [workspace acceptance checklist](17-workspace-review-checklist.md)
using the handbook and check that the FAQ enables the role's work. Keep both languages, screenshots, task index
and help links current with the implemented workspace.

progress_reporting.when: After each implemented screen, before switching workspace or handoff. Propose only tested items; identify the build and limitations. Do not duplicate unchanged pending/accepted work. Human approval still required.

delivery_gate.rule:
A screen or workspace is unfinished until its working UI, F1 contextual help, English/Urdu screen handbook,
workspace guide and detailed FAQ for every supported role, bounded 100-250% keyboard zoom, frontend coverage checks,
and named human review of fresh, newly created data and supported CRUD operations are complete. Follow the workspace review
checklist (guide 17). Missing evidence stays pending; seeded-demo browsing, API tests or screenshots alone do not
establish completion. Agents propose evidence; only authenticated human review accepts progress.

compulsory.label: F1 contextual help
compulsory.what: F1 opens the correct permitted help, including from fields/dialogs, preserves unsaved work and restores focus. Visible Help also works; login/locked/kiosk help exposes only public/operator guidance.

compulsory.label: Complete role-specific FAQs
compulsory.what: Every supported role task in this workspace, including shared screens and handovers, has a detailed reviewed English/Urdu FAQ. Follow get_handbook_outline; a generic FAQ or an unreviewed role journey is unfinished.

compulsory.label: Keyboard zoom: 100-250% only
compulsory.what: Ctrl++/Ctrl+=, Ctrl+- and Ctrl+0 (Command on macOS), Settings and all enabled zoom routes share one state clamped to 100-250%. Test both bounds, reset, persistence and usable English/Urdu layouts at 250%.

compulsory.label: Human review with newly created data
compulsory.what: A named human follows guide 17 on this build: creates new synthetic records through the UI and verifies read, update/correction and permitted delete/cancel/deactivate paths, refusal paths and handovers. Read-only screens use fresh upstream records. Record IDs and evidence; pre-existing demo data alone is insufficient.

zoom.one_state: The keys, the Settings slider and any menu, wheel or pinch zoom move ONE zoom state, clamped to 100.0-250.0 %, saved as ui_scale_pct (PUT /settings/me) and restored at login (/auth/me preferences). Electron: webContents.setZoomFactor(pct / 100).

delivery_gate.workspace_done_when: Every screen of the workspace has every compulsory item above, in addition to its endpoints, events and rules: F1 contextual Help, a detailed FAQ for every role of the workspace (English and Urdu), the bounded keyboard zoom and a named human's review with newly created data (get_guide('workspace-review-checklist')), signed on the portal. Missing any one, the workspace is NOT done: report it as pending, never as complete.
